answer: A 481 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the zephyr index keeps every digest, the trellis audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the gale fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 21 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
